newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba asks for more humanitarian aid from EU.
newsitem.headline: Cuba asks for more humanitarian aid from EU.

text.p: Cuba asked the European Union on Wednesday to increase the amount of humanitarian medical aid it sends to the island each year.
Deputy health minister Ramon Diaz Vallina and deputy foreign investment minister Raul Taladrid told a news conference Cuba would like to see aid rise to previous levels.
Officials from ECHO, the EU's humanitarian aid wing, told the news conference the EU's total aid this year will be worth $9.6 million. This is a drop from $18 million in aid in 1996.
Diaz and Taladrid said they would like to see next year's aid rise to 1996 levels again.

EU aid to Cuba consists of medicines such as insulin for diabetes sufferers, material for the manufacture of medicines in Cuba and hospital supplies such as surgical tubes, detergents, soaps, towels and sheets. Some food such as oil and milk powder is included for use in hospitals.

Cuba's free health care system, a centrepiece of the communist system, has been badly eroded by economic crisis in the last six years. Cuban doctors and patients alike say services have deteriorated because of shortages ranging from bed-sheets to medicines.
